text: Balance all internal graph forces by aim surface to prevent drift
description: Prevent internal layout interactions from translating the graph. Treat aim mass as displayed surface (radius²). For every hierarchy, collision, and semantic pair, derive one equal-and-opposite interaction and distribute resulting movement inversely to endpoint surface, so mA·ΔA + mB·ΔB = 0. Preserve normalized transported-flow strength on hierarchy connections. Global centering remains the only intentional external force. Add focused conservation tests for unequal aim sizes.
reflection: Mathematical audit: hierarchy links already split opposite endpoint movement by radius² surface mass, conserving mA·ΔA+mB·ΔB. Collision forces instead used radius weighting, and semantic forces used equal displacement, so the simulation mixed mass models and could translate the surface-weighted graph center. Updated collision and semantic interactions to use the same radius² invariant while preserving their equal-size relative correction. Replaced independent per-node movement clamping—which could break cancellation—with one shared scale across the whole frame. Normalized transported-flow strength remains unchanged. Only global centering and deliberate user/freeze constraints are external forces. Verification: graph-force tests 8/8 pass including unequal-surface conservation; frontend vue-tsc passes. Runtime visual acceptance remains required.

status.comment: All internal pair-force families now conserve the same surface-weighted center and shared clamping preserves cancellation; internally verified, awaiting Felix's visual runtime acceptance.
